mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over a 3-month period indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings growth and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of reduced corporate revenue growth and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (INDPRO > 105.0 and UNRATE < 4.5%), supply chain constraints and rising input costs erode corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO > 105.0 and UNRATE < 4.5, or the Rank IC for the regime condition falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 150,000 jobs per month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS growth exceeds 150,000, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% per annum signals the beginning of a monetary tightening cycle, which increases borrowing costs for corporations and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.0% signal a dual threat of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which compresses real interest rates and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: dual threat of tightening and inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise above thresholds, or the interaction term in a regression model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes characterized by rising housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) following a market correction, consumer confidence and spending rebound, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both rise, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
